intro.en: Music: instruments, concerts and the people who make them.

texto.en:
People: **el cantante**, **el compositor**, **el músico**, **el guitarrista**, **el pianista**, **el director de orquesta**, **el bailarín**. Words in -ista do not change: **la** guitarrista.

You **tocas** an instrument: la guitarra, el piano, el violín, **la batería**. You **cantas**, **bailas**, **compones** and **ensayas**.

A band **saca** un disco, **da** un concierto and **está de gira**. Music heard at a concert is **en directo**.

A song has **letra** and **música**. A song everyone knows is **un éxito**.

To say what music does to you, use the gustar pattern: **me emociona**, **me relaja**, **me pone** de buen humor, **me recuerda a** mi infancia.

**Tener buen oído** is to have a good ear. **Saberse** una canción **de memoria** is to know it by heart.

frases.es: Mi hermano toca la batería en un grupo desde hace diez años.
frases.en: My brother has played the drums in a band for ten years.

frases.es: Ensayan tres veces a la semana en un garaje de las afueras.
frases.en: They rehearse three times a week in a garage on the outskirts.
analisis: en un garaje de las afueras

frases.es: La cantante compone la música y él escribe casi todas las letras.
frases.en: The singer composes the music and he writes almost all the lyrics.

frases.es: El año pasado sacaron su primer disco, que fue un éxito inesperado.
frases.en: Last year they brought out their first album, which was an unexpected hit.

frases.es: Ahora están de gira y dan dos conciertos en directo cada semana.
frases.en: Now they are on tour and give two live concerts every week.

frases.es: Dice que lo que más le emociona es oír al público cantar sus canciones.
frases.en: He says that what moves him most is hearing the audience sing their songs.

Juega.en: Jugar is for sports and games.

Hace.en: Hacer is not used with instruments.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about a song that matters to you: what it says and what it reminds you of.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Talk aloud about the music you listen to, a concert you remember and an instrument you would like to play.
